lines.text: This bowler has never watched a single game of cricket.
Nobody ever taught it how to bowl.
At the start, it's hopeless.
Random speeds. Random lengths. It gets smashed all over the ground.
Inside, there's a tiny brain.
Eighteen inputs about the batter and the over. Four outputs: speed, length, line, and swing.
So I let evolution do the teaching.
A hundred and ninety two brains bowl against three different batters.
The best ones survive, and breed the next generation.
Fifteen hundred generations. More than eighty million deliveries.
And then, it started winning. A little too easily.
Look closer. Bouncer. Yorker. Bouncer. Yorker.
Flat out, then dead slow. Every dial pinned to the limit.
It hadn't learned to bowl. It had learned to cheat.
So I fixed the game. The batters now read patterns, and only two bouncers are allowed an over.
Then I started again. From nothing.
Generation one. Balls scattered everywhere.
Generation fifteen hundred. Every ball, on target.
This time, it learned real cricket.
Against the technician, a good length. Over and over. Until he edges one.
Against the tailender, full and straight. Trapped in front.
And the slogger? Yorkers. Right at the stumps.
You can even watch it think. Every neuron firing, ball by ball.
The final brain beats every specialist, against every batter.
And the cheater? Not even close.
No coaching. No examples. Just a reward, and evolution.
This is an AI that taught itself to bowl.
